parameters.content:
## Human approval gate for ClickUp

### Who's it for
Anyone who needs a person to sign off before an automation does something irreversible — sending client emails, issuing invoices, publishing content, provisioning access, letting an AI agent act.

Gmail, Slack and Telegram have native `sendAndWait` operations in n8n. **ClickUp does not.** This template fills that gap, so teams who already run their work in ClickUp can approve things where they already live instead of in a second tool.

### What it does
Install it once as a sub-workflow, then call it from any workflow that needs a sign-off. It creates a ClickUp task describing what needs approving, optionally announces it in a ClickUp Chat channel, then polls the task until a human moves it into one of three statuses. It returns a structured verdict to the caller and hands back the reviewer's own comment so a rejection or revision is actionable, not just a dead end.

### How it works
1. **Called** by a parent workflow with `approvalTitle`, `approvalSummary`, `referenceId` and `requestedBy`.
2. **Creates** a ClickUp task with the reviewer's instructions, a due date matching the timeout, and a link back to the n8n execution.
3. **Announces** it in a ClickUp Chat channel (optional).
4. **Polls** on a Wait loop. The execution is suspended between polls, so a request can sit for days at no cost.
5. **Classifies** each poll into approved, revision, rejected, timeout or pending — matching status names case-insensitively, because ClickUp lowercases them in API responses.
6. **Nudges** the reviewer with a task comment once the halfway point passes.
7. **Returns** one of four outcomes. Whichever branch runs last is what the parent receives.

### Requirements
A ClickUp API credential in n8n, one ClickUp list to hold approval tasks, and three statuses on that list. Core nodes only — nothing to install.

### Note on `decidedBy`
ClickUp's public v2 API does not expose status-change history, so this is best-effort: the author of the latest comment on revisions and rejections, the assignee on approvals. Treat it as a hint, not an audit trail.

## Placeholders — replace all six

Everything you must edit lives in the **Approval Settings** node. Nothing is hardcoded anywhere else in this workflow.

| Placeholder | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `PASTE_CLICKUP_LIST_ID` | Open the list in ClickUp — the last number in the URL `.../v/li/`**`901234567`** |
| `PASTE_CLICKUP_WORKSPACE_ID` | The first number after `app.clickup.com/`**`25658037`**`/...` |
| `PASTE_CLICKUP_CHANNEL_ID` | Open the Chat channel, copy link — the ID sits after `/chat/channels/`. Leave as-is if `notifyChannel` is false |
| `PASTE_CLICKUP_USER_ID_OR_LEAVE_BLANK` | Settings → Team → member → the numeric `id` from `GET /api/v2/team`. Blank means unassigned |
| `https://YOUR_N8N_INSTANCE_URL` | Your n8n base URL, no trailing slash. Left as-is, the execution backlink is simply omitted |
| `complete` / `needs revision` / `rejected` | The three status names **exactly as they exist on your list**. Case does not matter |

⚠️ **Never paste a ClickUp token into a header.** Every API node here uses n8n's ClickUp credential. If you migrated this from a workflow with a `pk_...` token in an `Authorization` header, rotate that token now — it has full workspace access.

## Setup

**1 · Prepare a ClickUp list.** Make a list to hold approval tasks and give it three statuses beyond the default open state — for example `complete`, `needs revision` and `rejected`. Any names work; you'll type yours into Approval Settings.

**2 · Add a ClickUp credential.** Settings → Apps → API Token in ClickUp, then create a ClickUp credential in n8n. Every HTTP node here already references it.

**3 · Fill in the placeholders** in Approval Settings (see the table above).

**4 · Tune the timing.** `pollIntervalMinutes` × `maxPollAttempts` is your SLA — the defaults give a 15-minute poll for 24 hours, with a nudge at the 12-hour mark. For same-day sign-offs try 5 and 96.

**5 · Test with the Manual Trigger.** Hit Test workflow, watch the task appear, then move it through each of the three statuses on separate runs to exercise all branches. Drop `pollIntervalMinutes` to 1 while testing.

**6 · Delete the demo nodes** and save. In the parent workflow, add an *Execute Sub-workflow* node pointing here, map the four input fields, and branch on the returned `decision`.

### 1 · Create the request

The task body tells the reviewer exactly which three statuses to use, so no separate training is needed. A due date matching the workflow's own timeout means ClickUp's native reminders do some of the chasing for you.

### 2 · Poll until a human decides

Wait suspends the execution rather than holding resources. `Classify Decision` uses `$runIndex` to count cycles, giving both the attempt counter and the timeout without any external state.

### 3 · Four outcomes, one return value

Only one branch ever runs, and a sub-workflow returns the output of its last executed node — so whichever `Return:` node fires is what the parent receives. Keep all four field sets identical in shape so the parent can read `decision` and `reviewerNotes` without knowing which path was taken.

### The pending branch closes the loop

Pending routes back to `Wait For Reviewer`, which is what makes this a polling loop rather than a one-shot check. The reminder fires exactly once because `Classify Decision` compares the attempt number for equality, not `>=`.

Want event-driven instead of polling? Switch the Wait node to *On webhook call*, and have a second workflow with a ClickUp Trigger on `taskStatusUpdated` call the resume URL. More setup, no polling cost.
